chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The believing servant does not cease to be written as a good-doer for as long as he is silent. So when he speaks, he is written either as a good-doer or an evil-doer.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of silence in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the spiritual discipline of the tongue, a core theme in Shia ethics. The hadith establishes a default state of merit for silence, which shifts to a variable state of reward or liability once speech begins, underscoring the believer's responsibility to guard their words. This reflects the broader Islamic principle that silence is not merely absence of speech but an active preservation of faith.
